problem: VLN work focuses on high-level reasoning, memory and decomposition, while the low-level action interface (discrete action tokens, waypoints, action chunks) is under-studied and entangled with instruction reasoning in standard evaluations. These interfaces specify only a current-state action, target or finite sequence, and do not describe how motion should vary across nearby locations or replanning frequencies.
motivation: Once the high-level sub-instruction is fixed, the choice of action representation still determines how intent becomes robot motion. Classical potential fields and velocity-space planners provide spatially indexed corrective guidance, and a prior BEV flow-field policy (CoFL) showed the benefit of dense workspace-level supervision but assumed a third-person global view. The paper brings this to first-person RGB-D onboard sensing.
key_idea: Predict a language-conditioned, spatially queryable 2D flow field over the robot's visible ego-centric ground sector from RGB-D and a local sub-instruction, and roll it out to obtain continuous trajectories, trained with dense potential-field supervision derived from replayed VLN-CE episodes.
insight: Dense supervision over the whole visible sector is what makes the field representation work: on-trajectory supervision gives SR 0.11, tube 0.13, full sector 0.35. The action module for STOP matters for task completion (SR 0.19 without it vs 0.35 with it), and depth FiLM lowers BSR from 0.27 to 0.15. Instruction-diverse augmentation gives only a moderate gain (SR 0.33 to 0.35). The field's advantage is largest over immediate-action baselines at low planner frequency.
method: Sector flow field: a velocity field v(q|I,D,l) in Cartesian ego ground-plane coordinates, queried at normalized polar sector coordinates q=(theta~, r~) in [-1,1]x[0,1] aligned with camera FoV; trajectory obtained by integrating the field.

Encoder: unfrozen SigLIP 2 vision/text towers; depth patchified by a conv and injected into visual tokens via bounded residual FiLM (iota_max=0.1, eta_max=0.05); transformer decoder-style fusion with vision tokens as queries and text as keys/values.

Query decoder: Gaussian Fourier embedding of sector coordinates, cross-attention-only decoder layers over fused context, and magnitude (softplus) and unit-direction heads; the field is cached on a 40x40 polar grid.
Action module: learnable action-ID queries decode STOP probability, used only as a termination gate.
Loss: cosine direction loss plus squared magnitude loss (distance-to-go scale) at area-uniform stratified sector queries, plus action cross-entropy.

Rollout: 100-step forward Euler integration in Cartesian space with bilinear interpolation on the cached grid and a bounded inverse-time rescaling s(j,T) (beta=0.5, alpha=10); tracked by a shared pure-pursuit controller.

Supervision pipeline: replay R2R-CE/RxR-CE, align frames to Fine-Grained R2R / Landmark-RxR sub-instructions, add K-slot object/region/terminal alternatives, and build a potential (cost-weighted Dijkstra geodesic attraction plus distance-transform repulsion) whose negative gradient gives dense flow, trajectory and action targets.

Benchmark: continuous-time Habitat (60 Hz physics, 30 Hz RGB-D, planner at 2/5/10 Hz, zero-order hold) with oracle-pose-selected sub-instructions and one shared velocity controller for all interfaces.

setting.backbone: SigLIP 2 (fine-tuned) + fusion transformer + query-based sector decoder (trained); StreamVLN variant with a 2-layer CoFL-S decoder
setting.model_size: Head 30.28M params (excluding SigLIP 2 encoder); StreamVLN variant uses a 3584-d backbone
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE training episodes replayed in Habitat with Fine-Grained R2R / Landmark-RxR sub-instructions plus procedural object/region/terminal instruction alternatives; 3,758,511 samples (2,400,923 anchor-only); StreamVLN variant uses 571,546 decisions
setting.observation: ego-centric RGB-D (224x224, depth clipped 0-5 m) plus local sub-instruction
setting.action_space: continuous trajectory from sector-field rollout tracked by pure pursuit into (v, omega) velocity commands, max 0.5 m/s and 1.0 rad/s; discrete STOP gate
setting.privileged: Oracle agent pose used to select the aligned sub-instruction at test time (sim); operator-assigned sub-instructions in real world; the Waypoint baseline uses a GT navmesh planner (not CoFL-S)

numbers_note: Sim metrics are printed as fractions (SR 0.37 = 37%) and NE in meters; kept exactly as printed. Real-world results: SR 0.75, CT 0.42, T-S 111.50 s, PL-S 42.43 m, latency 143.29 ms (8 sequences x 3 repeats, own robot), not a canonical benchmark.
results: Under matched encoders and training, CoFL-S beats Action Token, Action Chunk, Waypoint+GT Planner and Velocity Regression on NE/OS/SR/SPL at 2/5/10 Hz. For example, R2R-CE at 2 Hz reaches SR 0.37 vs best baseline 0.28 (Action Chunk); RxR-CE SR is 0.33-0.34 vs at most 0.27. In zero-shot real-world runs, SR is 0.75 vs 0.46 (Action Token) and 0.33 (Action Chunk). Plugged into StreamVLN it keeps SR (0.58 vs 0.57) and cuts BSR from 0.07 to 0.02.
limitations: Assumes a local sub-instruction is provided (oracle pose alignment in sim, operator in real); no long-horizon decomposition, memory or exploration.
Field is a 2D camera-centered ground-plane sector: no 3D collision or vertical clearance; semantic grounding errors and targets leaving the view remain unrecovered.

Absolute success is low under the benchmark (SR 0.33-0.37), it is a custom continuous-time benchmark on a subset of val-unseen (not comparable with standard VLN-CE), and real-world comparison covers only two baselines with higher latency.
